Subject: Re: Quickstart templates docs — review loop (safe defaults, PII, observability setup)

Left comments in the doc, but capturing the main requests here so nothing gets lost:

PII / logging:
- Please avoid phrasing like “PII-safe by default” or anything that reads like a compliance guarantee.
- Be explicit: templates emit structured logs + traces; they do NOT intentionally log prompt content or document chunks by default.
- Add a short warning that users should treat prompts, retrieved context, tool outputs, and user messages as potentially sensitive and avoid logging them unless they have a clear business need + appropriate controls.
- Where we show example logs, make sure the sample fields are limited to request_id/tenant_id/route/model/error_class/latency, etc. No “user_message” fields.

Secrets:
- In the “Local dev” section, clarify that .env is for local only, should not be committed, and keys should be rotated if exposed.

Observability:
- Ensure we don’t imply that Redwood Console automatically receives customer app logs/traces. We provide the telemetry contract and optional exporter configuration; customer must configure where telemetry is sent.

I’ll sync with Marcus on wording if helpful.

-Naomi

Subject: Re: Quickstart templates docs — review loop (safe defaults, PII, observability setup)

Added comments mainly in the “Production defaults” and “429s” sections.

Key asks from Product:
- The page currently says “automatic retries” without calling out scope. We should say “retries for retryable transport/429 errors with exponential backoff + jitter” and mention “non-idempotent operations should use idempotency keys” (or link to our SDK guidance).
- For rate limits: avoid “Redwood will retry for you.” The template/SDK handles certain cases, but customers still need to handle 429s at the app layer and cap concurrency.
- Make sure “timeouts” are described as a requirement, not optional: API calls should always have bounded timeouts; streaming connections should have heartbeat / disconnect handling.

Also: in Observability, please add one sentence connecting token usage metrics to Console cost breakdowns (without overpromising). Something like: “When request tagging is enabled, you can correlate cost/latency by route/model in Console.”

Thanks,
Nikhil

From: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 11:24 AM
Subject: Re: Quickstart templates docs — review loop (safe defaults, PII, observability setup)

I can take the edits, but I need clarity on one doc point that got a few conflicting comments:

Observability setup currently says:
“Enable OpenTelemetry and see traces in the Redwood Console.”

My understanding is:
- Redwood Console shows request-level telemetry for Redwood API calls (and token usage/cost), but it’s not a general-purpose APM ingest for the customer’s own service traces/logs.
- The templates also emit OTel spans/metrics locally so customers can export to their own collector (Datadog/OTel Collector/etc.).

Proposed rewrite:
“Templates emit OpenTelemetry traces/metrics you can export to your APM. Redwood Console provides inference-level observability (latency, tokens, errors) for Redwood API requests and can correlate to your request_id.”

Is that accurate enough for launch copy?

Also adding a PII block (per Naomi) below the first code example on “Structured logs.”

-Wei

Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 12:08 PM
Subject: Re: Quickstart templates docs — review loop (safe defaults, PII, observability setup)

Wei’s proposed rewrite is directionally correct.

Two tweaks so we don’t confuse people:
1) Say “Redwood Console provides inference observability for Redwood requests (model, route, token usage, latency, error class)” — emphasize it’s not collecting arbitrary application logs.
2) Add a short “Join key” sentence: “Use request_id and traceparent propagation to join your app traces with Redwood request events.”

If you want a concrete snippet, you can include something like:
- set OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=quickstart-rag,service.version=…
- propagate traceparent header when calling Redwood

We should avoid a step that requires users to already run an OTel Collector for “first 15 minutes” success. Maybe:
- default to console-friendly request_id + logs
- put OTel exporter setup under “Optional: connect to your APM”

Marissa

+1 to the direction.

Concrete wording suggestions (feel free to lift):

PII guidance block (short):
“Do not log raw prompts, retrieved document text, user messages, or tool outputs by default. Treat them as sensitive. If you choose to log content for debugging, ensure you have appropriate access controls, retention limits, and redaction.”

Safe defaults:
- In “Retries”, add “bounded” and “fail fast” language. Something like: “Retries are capped; requests have timeouts; repeated failures should surface as errors rather than retrying indefinitely.”

Secrets:
- Please add a line: “Never paste API keys into screenshots, issues, or chat logs.” (Support has been seeing this.)

Also I’d remove the phrase “secure-by-default” in the hero section. It tends to trigger compliance questions. Maybe “production-minded defaults” instead.

-Marcus
